newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk refinery sees 97 net down PLN 20 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk refinery sees 97 net down PLN 20 mln.

text.p: The two-month shutdown at Poland's Gdansk refinery will cut its net profits by 20 million zlotys to 84 million zlotys this year against a 46 million profit in 1996, the firm's head said.
"The two month break will cut this year's profit by 20 million to 84 million," Wlodzimierz Dyrka told a news conference on Thursday.
He said the company's net profit would be higher than last year thanks to the freeing of fuel prices earlier in 1997. But he said the refinery had no immediate plans to raise prices.
"We do not plan a fuel price rise in the near future. The price of fuel in Poland is now more dependent on the zloty exchange rate than on the prices on world markets," Dyrka said.

Dyrka said the refinery spent 100 million zlotys on modernisation during the two-month shutdown for maintenance and upgrading work at the country's second largest refinery. As a result of the work, the refinery's crude processing capacity of 3.5 million tonnes annually. It will invest another 110 million this year.
The refinery wants to reach a processing capacity of 4.5 million tone crude processing capacity in 1999 after further investment of 800 million zlotys in 1998 and 180 million in 1999.
